Reviewed 2026-10-02 under the run-eval skill. UID `636a830d-18b9-49c7-b7eb-f417d45e949c`.

Raw root (R): `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/gedcom-cpp-gpt-5.6-luna-max/gedcom-cpp/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-luna_max/eval1/run1`. ## Disposition

**Qualifies for publication unchanged: 164/212 (77.36%), 48 failures.** The submission is substantial, built successfully, and completed voluntarily. The failures predominantly reflect overly restrictive or incomplete context-sensitive GEDCOM validation, not absent implementation, build failure, timeout, quota failure, or external-reference contamination. Preserve frozen scoring. No submission was executed on the host, and this review did not change raw evidence, tests, prompts, scoring, or publication files.

## Failure accounting: all 48 observations

These counts partition the failed test-report entries; they are not 48 independent implementation defects. In compound fixtures, the first statically identifiable rejection is used rather than attributing failure to every feature named by the test.

| Observations | Affected tests | Source cause and public requirement |
|---:|---|---|
| 16 | `test_data_types.py:52` seven `test_date_value_forms_are_accepted` parameters and `:89` Julian BCE; `test_parse.py:21,34,56` three sample-dataset tests; `test_gedzip.py:27,49` two successful archive tests; `test_schema.py:9,26`; `test_validation.py:272` leading-at rendering | The shared fixtures contain `BIRT Y`. `expectedValue` at 2068-2076 returns `ValueKind::None` for event tags; `validateValue` at 2523 rejects any nonempty payload. Public `#INDIVIDUAL_EVENT_STRUCTURE` explicitly allows `[Y|<NULL>]` for BIRT. These are **not eight proven date-parser failures**, nor proof that ZIP, schema, multiline, or at-escaping itself is broken. |
| 2 | `test_parse.py:74,87` extended sample inspect/roundtrip | `allowedChild` 2147-2150 applies source-citation children to root SOUR records, rejecting their TITL before the fixture's later BIRT Y. Public `#SOURCE_RECORD` explicitly permits TITL, AUTH, ABBR, PUBL, etc. Root source and citation contexts are conflated. |

The first 16 failures explain why unrelated-looking date, schema, render and archive tests all fail together. Some negative tests containing the same BIRT Y may also pass by rejecting for the wrong reason; a passing assertion is not independent evidence of the intended deeper validation.

## Canonical representation caveat

The three VOID failures are observable frozen-suite incompatibilities, but should not be described simply as failure to support void pointers. The source deliberately supports them using JSON null, and the transcript says so. The technical requirements specify a generic tree with `payload: string or null`, but do not expressly state whether the GEDCOM null-pointer spelling must remain the string `"@VOID@"` or be normalized to JSON null. The test fixtures preserve the spelling. A future version should explicitly document this mapping (including render acceptance) to avoid conflating a canonicalization choice with failure to parse a legal GEDCOM pointer. Do not change this run's score or pause the collection because of this caveat. The other mapped failures have direct public grammar or example support.

Reviewed canonical command/message progression, relevant command outputs, failure reports and source validation paths. The agent read the local prompt and supplied HTML extensively, wrote its own implementation, then performed local builds and targeted self-tests. Transcript item_10 is a recovered model-authored HTML-extraction KeyError; item_39 is the initial compile failure, followed by successful builds. Item_122 fails to open a removed local `zip-response.json` fixture; it is a failed verification command, not an infrastructure interruption or proof of a ZIP failure. Subsequent fresh build item_148 and final build item_150 succeed.

The final item_151 message (transcript line 322) claims implementation of all requested actions and lists validation, rendering, UTF-8, continuation, pointers and archive support. Four action implementations and a successful build support the broad feature-presence claim, but the statement is not evidence of complete GEDCOM compliance. The preceding completion message (line 319) describes successful self-checks, not hidden-suite success. Report **claims complete; incomplete correctness not acknowledged**, with the concrete limitations above; do not call this a stub or fabricated build claim.

The canonical turn completes after the final message, with no request for user input or forced interruption. Network audit independently groups to 162 allowed chatgpt.com and one allowed ab.chatgpt.com API connection, plus ten denied OpenAI asset requests. There are no allowed external-reference destinations or retrieval commands in the reviewed command inventory. Network condition is api-only. The sibling `accounting-review.md` establishes 149 tools (147 canonical underlying items plus two session-proven rejected patch calls), exact cumulative tokens and $0.691752; its narrowly scoped diagnostic fingerprint covers recovered patch-context errors, not missing execution. All four actions are implemented, but overstrict/context-insensitive GEDCOM validation rejects legal BIRT Y, optional record identifiers, empty EVEN text, source-record fields and extension-defined descendants; time/age grammar and GEDZIP file/backlink validation also remain incomplete.
